issues.what: Calendar collapses: gala is three weeks away in ch2, six days away in ch4, seven days away again in ch8-9, yet ch10 has ten pieces 'found each Thursday'; only two returns ever happen on the page.
issues.quote: I propose a gala. Three weeks.

issues.what: Case 4 has been empty since 1994, but ch3's register records all eleven recovered in 1995 and ch4 shows Bashir swapping returns for fakes on display; the core mechanic of the mystery contradicts itself.
issues.quote: Case 4, empty since she was eight years old, was not empty.

issues.what: The decisive proof makes no sense: a 1994 receipt from Lodhi to Sethi sealed in a plaster plug inside the Lodhi foot; it also re-runs the KTS ring-stamp reveal from ch8 as if new, and meta text 'evidence bag from Chapter 1' is pasted into prose.
issues.quote: Then she held up the evidence bag from Chapter 1

issues.what: The expert is male Dr. Ansari in ch2, a small woman Dr. Qureshi in ch7, then Qureshi is 'he' in ch10; the six-toed foot is on the Case 6 torso in ch7 and a separate loose piece at Lodhi's in ch8.
issues.quote: Dr. Qureshi stood beside him, arms folded, ready with his verdict.

issues.what: Bashir Masih is Christian yet says he prayed Fajr; his account also flips (ch1: case empty at two, ch2: case full). Brief says avoid misrepresenting religious minorities.
issues.quote: I prayed at two. Fajr is early in winter.

issues.what: Mehru's age drifts: eight in 1994 (ch1), fourteen in 1995 (ch3), neither fits the brief's 34.
issues.quote: She had been fourteen that autumn

issues.what: Pervaiz's scratched ledger name was a single letter S in ch6, becomes 'Lodhi' in ch8; threads left hanging: the fresh red paint curl, the anonymous text about keys, 'my abba never ate fish'.
issues.quote: You said your abba's ledger had a name. You said Lodhi.

issues.what: Crossword clue drifts (SEVEN ACROSS, then One across); the final seven-letter answer is BASHIR, six letters. Ch10 also has Case 4 'open one inch' though ch1 says it was locked.
issues.quote: Seven letters. Cleared at last.

issues.what: Three chapters share the title 'The Urdu Newspaper' (5, 6, 8); a real newspaper is named (Daily Express); board members drink wine at a Lahore museum gala.
issues.quote: The newspaper was today's Daily Express, Urdu

praise: Bashir is a lovely creation, and the red-over-brick-dust accession numbers are a clever, fair clue; the opening at 3 a.m. in the fog is a strong hook.

issues.what: Hatching secret contradicts itself: ch1 has Sayed bringing the box home and Hoda carrying an 'egg box', ch4 says the egg came from their own hen while Sayed was in hospital; the payoff is never stated to anyone on the page.
issues.quote: Everyone had seen Sayed bring the box home.

issues.what: The telling clue (red tape) is tied to a delivery box never seen before, instead of the phone planted in ch1; Mahrous quotes the biscuit tin, which Hoda never told him.
issues.quote: She had seen that tape on Amr's delivery box when he mended a loose wire

issues.what: The false entry's ring ends 1187, the same digits as Sultan's own ring, a false clue the story never pays off.
issues.quote: Ring EG 2026 1187.

issues.what: Sultan is identified by a white wing edge never mentioned before, not the narrow face and gold-dust eye set up in ch2.
issues.quote: the white edge on his left wing

issues.what: Chapter titles don't match content (ch3 'The Bent Nail' is the race list, ch4 'The 2026 Ring' is the rooftop wait, ch5 'The Trap Hook' is the homecoming).
issues.quote: The Bent Nail

issues.what: Amr heard her plan at the coffee house at noon, not 'last night'.
issues.quote: in front of the whole coffee house last night

issues.what: The Hussein mosque is in Islamic Cairo, not Shubra; Ahly shirt is a real club brand; Hag/Hagg and Kasr El Ainy/Aini, Ya Sattar/Ya satr, tameya/taameya spelling drift.
issues.quote: The adhan from the Hussein mosque had finished

issues.what: Amr says leaving the trap open would look 'like someone forced it', but nothing was forced.
issues.quote: Like someone forced it.

fix: Ch1: Sultan's egg kept warm in a biscuit tin, the Tanta story only heard, not seen; ch5: red tape tied to Amr's phone, Mahrous doesn't quote the biscuit tin, Hoda states the hatching truth, Sultan known by his gold-dust eye; ch3 false ring renumbered; retitle ch3-5; spelling/brand fixes.
praise: The rooftop world is vivid and warm, and the fair-play homing logic lands: a stolen bird wearing another man's ring drops onto the widow's loft.

issues.what: Timeline breaks the fair-play clue: the narration says Ergash began building at seven thirty, but his walkthrough (and the rice going on at seven thirty) has meat at four, carrots at six.
issues.quote: At seven thirty Ergash began to build.

issues.what: The deduction names three suspects but never rules out Mukaddas or Karimov; only the bandage hints at Sardor.
issues.quote: Only three. Karimov-aka with quince. Mukaddasxon with bread.

issues.what: Sardor still has his knife in hand at the table hours after he finished cutting.
issues.quote: but his knife was still in his hand

issues.what: Brief says the skimmer and debt are handed over quietly; here it is announced to the courtyard, which risks humiliating the teen (an Avoid item).
issues.quote: Ergash held out his long iron skimmer to him.

issues.what: Mukaddas wears an ikat dress and headscarf in magenta and green per the brief; typos 'Sixty three', 'Three o clock'.
issues.quote: Three o clock, fire.

fix: Ch1: set the build to start at four; add Ergash's elimination of Mukaddas (before carrots) and Karimov (quince from a plate he held); drop the knife at the table; make the skimmer handover quiet; costume and typo fixes.
praise: A perfect little fair-play puzzle built from the real craft of plov, with a generous, funny, very human resolution.
